## Current position

**Postdoctoral researcher** · June 2025–present  
Theoretical Quantum Technology group, Institute for Applied Physics, TU Darmstadt. I work in Claudiu Genes’s group, where I study how decoherence and atom loss affect collective light emission.

## Education

**Dr. rer. nat. in Physics** · October 2020–May 2025  
Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), *magna cum laude*. I carried out my doctoral research at FAU and the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light under the supervision of Claudiu Genes and Kai P. Schmidt. My dissertation was [*Quantum Optics with Atoms and Molecules*](publications.qmd#quantum-optics-with-atoms-and-molecules).

During my doctorate I was a member of the Integrated Research Training Group of [QuCoLiMa (Quantum Cooperativity of Light and Matter, TRR 306)](https://www.lightmatter.fau.de/people/early-career-researchers/). I served as a doctoral student representative from October 2023.

**M.Sc. in Physics** · July 2017–September 2020  
FAU, with distinction. My [master’s thesis](files/2020_Masterthesis_Bassler.pdf) studied the effect of domain walls in bilayer graphene in an external magnetic field.

**B.Sc. in Physics** · October 2013–July 2017  
FAU, Elite Degree Programme in Physics.

## Teaching and supervision

I was a teaching assistant for seven quantum mechanics courses between 2016 and 2024. I also taught tutorials on topics including condensed matter and quantum optics, quantum and classical algorithms, and the theoretical physics of climate change.

I have co-supervised master’s and doctoral research in collective quantum optics, including Dicke superradiance, and supervised visiting doctoral students. My current student supervision also includes four-wave mixing in hollow-core fiber.
